# Resource: stripe_entitlements_feature

A feature a product can grant, identified by a unique `lookup_key`. Set `active` to `false` to archive the feature; an archived feature cannot be updated or reactivated, and its `lookup_key` cannot be used again.

~> Stripe cannot delete an entitlement feature; set `active` to `false` to archive one, which cannot be undone. `terraform destroy`, and a change that would replace the entitlements feature, fail at plan time. To stop managing an entitlements feature, remove it from the state as [Removing from State](#removing-from-state) shows; it stays in the Stripe account.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "stripe_entitlements_feature" "advanced_search" {
  lookup_key = "advanced_search"
  name       = "Advanced search"
}
```

## Argument Reference

The following arguments are required:

* `lookup_key` - (Required) A unique key you provide as your own system identifier. This may be up to 80 characters. Changing it fails the plan, because this resource cannot be replaced.
* `name` - (Required) The feature's name, for your own purpose, not meant to be displayable to the customer.

The following arguments are optional:

* `active` - (Optional) Inactive features cannot be attached to new products and will not be returned from the features list endpoint. Default: not sent. Removing it from the configuration stops sending it, and the next apply records the value Stripe holds.
* `metadata` - (Optional) Set of key-value pairs that you can attach to an object. This can be useful for storing additional information about the object in a structured format.

## Attribute Reference

This resource exports the following attributes in addition to the arguments above:

* `id` - Unique identifier for the object.
* `livemode` - If the object exists in live mode, the value is `true`. If the object exists in test mode, the value is `false`.

## Timeouts

[Configuration options](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/syntax#operation-timeouts) are set with the `timeouts` attribute, for example `timeouts = { create = "5m" }`:

* `create` - (Default `20m`)
* `delete` - (Default `20m`)
* `update` - (Default `20m`)

## Removing from State

To stop managing an entitlements feature whose destroy is refused, remove it from the state without destroying it. In Terraform 1.7 and later, and OpenTofu 1.10 and later, replace the `resource` block with a [`removed` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/block/removed) and apply:

```terraform
removed {
  from = stripe_entitlements_feature.advanced_search

  lifecycle {
    destroy = false
  }
}
```

Using `terraform state rm`:

```console
% terraform state rm stripe_entitlements_feature.advanced_search
```

The entitlements feature stays in the Stripe account. Replacing one with `terraform apply -replace` or `terraform taint` fails in the same way, at apply.

## Import

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, and in OpenTofu, use an [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) to import an entitlements feature using its ID. For example:

```terraform
import {
  to = stripe_entitlements_feature.advanced_search
  id = "feat_123"
}
```

In Terraform v1.12.0 and later, and in OpenTofu v1.12.0 and later, the `import` block can use the `identity` attribute instead. For example:

```terraform
import {
  to = stripe_entitlements_feature.advanced_search
  identity = {
    id = "feat_123"
  }
}
```

### Identity Schema

#### Required

* `id` (String) The Stripe ID of the entitlements feature.

Using `terraform import`, import an entitlements feature using its ID. For example:

```console
% terraform import stripe_entitlements_feature.advanced_search feat_123
```
